identity.title: Meet one life.
identity.body: Begin with the animal — then keep population, pod, ecotype and live location unknown until a source supports them.
identity.audioLabel: DEEP WATER BED · PROCEDURAL · NOT FIELD AUDIO

hotspots.label: ORCA
hotspots.detail: Canonical identity is Orcinus orca. This controlled illustration is not a photograph and does not identify a population, pod or ecotype.

hotspots.label: SOCIAL LIFE
hotspots.detail: Orca populations can differ in calls, diet, behaviour and habitat use. The interface does not infer those traits for an unidentified animal.

hotspots.label: OPEN OCEAN
hotspots.detail: The species occurs across all oceans. This scene is illustrative context, not a complete range map or live position.

dependency.title: What it eats depends on who it is.
dependency.body: Follow the animal into a population-specific food web. Different groups can specialise in different prey and hunting strategies.

hotspots.label: PREY
hotspots.detail: Prey specialisation is population-specific. A generic species page cannot say what an unidentified orca eats.

hotspots.label: FORAGING CULTURE
hotspots.detail: Groups may use distinct hunting strategies. The Journey keeps this as population-level context, not an individual diagnosis.

hotspots.label: EVIDENCE
hotspots.detail: Use the evidence control for the exact source and limitation attached to this dependency node.

habitat.title: A whale is never only a whale.
habitat.body: Pull back into shelves, fjords and open water. Place matters because prey, movement and human pressure are not uniform across the ocean.

hotspots.label: COASTAL SHELF
hotspots.detail: Some coastal groups follow prey along shelves and fjords. This is general context and not a complete range statement.

hotspots.label: FJORD
hotspots.detail: Fjords can be important to some coastal populations. The Journey does not transfer this habitat use to every orca population.

hotspots.label: OPEN WATER
hotspots.detail: Other groups range across open water. Species-level occurrence does not establish abundance, movement route or present location.

pressure.title: The ocean gets louder.
pressure.body: Noise and vessel interaction affect some killer-whale populations. The strength and consequence of that pressure depend on population, place and exposure.

hotspots.label: VESSEL TRAFFIC
hotspots.detail: Vessel interaction is documented for some populations. This prototype does not assert a universal exposure level.

hotspots.label: UNDERWATER NOISE
hotspots.detail: Noise can interfere with communication and hunting for some populations. Magnitude and consequence remain place- and population-specific.

hotspots.label: PREY AVAILABILITY
hotspots.detail: Reduced prey availability is another documented pressure category for some populations. It is not inferred from this scene.

hotspots.label: EVIDENCE
hotspots.detail: The evidence control exposes the source and the exact limitation carried by the canonical Living Systems node.

response.title: Response starts with specificity.
response.body: No single intervention protects every orca. A credible response starts by identifying the population, place, evidence and competent actor.
response.audioLabel: OPEN WATER RETURN + FORWARD MOTIF · PROCEDURAL

hotspots.label: IDENTIFY POPULATION
hotspots.detail: Population identity changes which pressure and response evidence is relevant.

hotspots.label: REDUCE DISTURBANCE
hotspots.detail: Disturbance reduction is a response class, not a claim of effectiveness for an unspecified population or place.

hotspots.label: PREY + HABITAT
hotspots.detail: Prey and habitat can matter to response design. A concrete action requires local science and accountable institutions.

hotspots.label: RESPONSIBLE ACTOR
hotspots.detail: Actor categories are not partnerships or endorsements. Specific organisations require verification before public attribution.

items.label: Population
items.note: Must be identified where response depends on it

items.label: Actor
items.note: Competence and authority must be verified
